decision_note: Primary Silene floral-colour selection study evaluates indirect/direct selection in a biotic context that includes pollinators and antagonists; retain to resolve whether both agents act on the same colour/trait coordinate.
Flower-colour molecular-mechanism/natural-selection review rather than a focal primary pollinator-antagonist experiment.

Primary Primula farinosa study links morph-specific pollen limitation, grazer/seed-predator damage and selection on floral-display/pollination-efficiency traits across three populations; retain for same-axis/context adjudication.
Primary thesis study explicitly measures floral-head traits, pollinator visitation, seed predators and developed-seed reproductive success in Helianthus grosseserratus.

Primary common-milkweed selection study measures floral attractive/defensive traits, pollinator activity, herbivory and fruit-based fitness; retain to resolve whether the antagonist route is attached to the same floral coordinate.
Primary floral-trait selection study quantifies pollinator- and seed-predator-associated selection under snowmelt/precipitation contexts; strong candidate for repeated total-selection effects.
Title and study design explicitly concern natural selection on Protea inflorescence colour by pollinators and seed predators; retain for full same-coordinate/fitness adjudication.
Book chapter synthesizing non-pollinator agents of floral-trait selection rather than a focal primary empirical study.
Focal selection coordinate is prey choice/ontogenetic diet of flower-dwelling spiders, not variation in a plant floral signal trait.
Claytonia floral-colour selection is framed around herbivores and pathogens; no focal pollinator component is identified in the title/abstract evidence.
Duplicate/alternate DOI record of the Claytonia herbivore/pathogen floral-colour study; primary title/abstract exclusion is absence of a focal pollinator component.

Primary two-population Primula secundiflora selection study includes legitimate and illegitimate/nectar-hole bumblebee behavior plus female-fitness selection; retain because exploiter role is plausible but role-dependent.

Primary Penstemon scent-selection study measures phenotypic selection and reproductive success but explicitly calls pollinator- and antagonist-mediated selection a future research need rather than measuring an antagonist route.
Primary floral-colour transition-zone study explicitly compares pollinator, herbivore and climatic selective pressures; retain for shared-trait and repeated-context adjudication.

Primary Dactylorhiza experiment quantifies pollinator-mediated selection on floral traits and records insect fruit herbivory affecting developing fruits; retain to resolve matched antagonist contribution.
Linum pubescens study directly tests pollinator-mediated selection; florivores/other antagonists are proposed as possible unmeasured agents rather than a measured antagonist component.
Primary Primula alpicola floral-selection study includes pollinator-mediated selection and biotic damage/seed-predator context; uncertainty resolves to full text for matched-agent adjudication.
Primary Lobelia cardinalis study directly compares pollinator- and herbivore-mediated selection on floral traits and seed-production fitness.
Penstemon experiment directly manipulates pollination and reviews herbivore selection in other studies, but does not measure a focal antagonist component in the primary experiment.
Primary Trillium discolor study explicitly estimates pollinator-mediated selection and tests whether natural antagonist damage alters selection on the same floral traits.
Molecular-evolution study of amino-acid/substrate discrimination in a plant volatile-producing enzyme; no focal plant-pollinator selection component is measured.
Primary Glechoma experiment links selective nectar robbing to legitimate-pollinator switching, pollination rates and seed set; retain for role/trait-coordinate adjudication.

Primary Comastoma factorial experiment crosses nectar robbing with pollination mode and measures developing ovules, mature seeds, seed weight and germination; retain for exploiter/reproductive-outcome coding.
Primary Impatiens experiment manipulates pollinator access and foliar herbivory and measures seed-based selection on floral traits; retain despite a null herbivory effect.
Primary Brassica cage experiment exposes plants to bumblebees, cabbage butterflies, or both and analyzes selection on floral signals; direct pollinator-antagonist selection candidate.

Hesperis dissertation primarily assesses floral-scent variation, fitness and potential pollinator-mediated selection; herbivore attraction is proposed as a possible cost rather than a measured antagonist selection component.

Primary Ruellia study evaluates floral evolution under competing selective pressures after hawkmoth-pollination loss and includes seed-predator/visitor context; retain for full agent/outcome adjudication.
Primary thesis explicitly targets the relative roles of herbivore- and pollinator-mediated selection on floral display in Lythrum salicaria; retain.
Primary Silene F2-hybrid field study measures floral traits, pollinator visitation, seed set and Hadena seed predation on the same recombinant trait variation; retain.
Primary dissertation on variation, agents and consequences of floral-trait selection; title/metadata are broad but potentially contain relevant primary chapters, so uncertainty resolves to full text.
Common-morning-glory experiment crosses pollinator restriction with abiotic water deficit; no animal antagonist/exploiter component is manipulated or measured.
New Phytologist Commentary on another floral-scent selection paper, not a focal primary empirical study.
